;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**Afghan officials say a government strike Sunday night on a militant facility in [[Musa Qala District]], [[Helmand Province]], killed 35 or more civilians at a wedding party nearby. The Afghan [[Ministry of Defense (Afghanistan)|Defence Ministry]] says the operation targeted a training facility for suicide bombers and it killed 22 members of the [[Taliban]]. The Taliban say 18 members of the Afghan forces were killed. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attack/at-least-35-people-at-wedding-party-killed-during-nearby-afghan-army-raid-idUSKBN1W80MI (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*In a rare joint press release, European [[Automotive industry|car makers]] warn that a [[no-deal Brexit]], introducing administrative hassle and tariffs, would have a "seismic" impact on [[Frictionless market|frictionless]] trading conditions and that it would deal a "severe" blow to the industry's [[just-in-time manufacturing]] supply chains, also potentially affecting "consumer choice and affordability on both sides of [[English Channel|the Channel]]". [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/sep/23/no-deal-brexit-will-have-seismic-impact-says-european-car-industry (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]
*[[Thomas Cook Group#Collapse|Collapse of Thomas Cook]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] travel company [[Thomas Cook Group|Thomas Cook]] enters [[Liquidation#Compulsory liquidation|compulsory liquidation]], leaving 150,000 British holidaymakers stranded abroad and endangering 22,000 jobs worldwide. In response, the [[UK government]] and the [[Civil Aviation Authority (United Kingdom)|Civil Aviation Authority]] launches Operation Matterhorn, the largest repatriation in the UK's peacetime history. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-49791249 (BBC News)] [https://www.gov.uk/government/news/government-and-uk-caa-launches-largest-repatriation-in-peacetime-history-after-collapse-of-thomas-cook (Gov.uk)]
**[[Tunisia]]n [[tourism minister]] [[René Trabelsi]] says Thomas Cook owes Tunisian hotels [[euro|€]]60 million for stays in July and August, with 4,500 customers still in the country. Tourism is a [[Tourism in Tunisia|major component]] of the [[economy of Tunisia|national economy]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thomas-cook-grp-investment-tunisia-ho/thomas-cook-owes-tunisian-hotels-60-million-euros-minister-idUSKBN1W810R (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Southeast Asian haze]]
**Raging [[wildfire]]s in [[Indonesia]] cause the sky to turn red over much of [[Sumatra]]. The phenomenon is a result of [[Rayleigh scattering]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-49793047 (BBC News)]
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**[[Boeing]] announces each relative of victims of two air disasters will be paid [[US$]]144,500 by the aircraft manufacturer, and will not have to waive their right to litigate to receive the money. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-airplane-victims/boeing-to-pay-737-max-crash-victims-families-144500-each-idUSKBN1W8288 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[Doctors Without Borders]] alleges the [[World Health Organisation]] is rationing [[vaccination|vaccines]] for [[Ebola]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] despite adequate resources. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190923-dr-congo-msf-doctors-without-borders-accuses-who-rationing-ebola-vaccine (France 24)]

;International relations
*[[Iran]] says a [[UK]]-flagged ship seized several months ago is free to depart. [[Ship prefix|MV]] ''Stena Impero'', an oil tanker, was captured in response to the seizure of an Iranian oil tanker in [[Gibraltar]] over allegations it was carrying fuel to [[Syria]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/british-ship-iran-seized-us-tanker-latest-a9116561.html (''The Independent'')]

;Law and crime
*After "seriously considering feedback from different parties who feel objections on some substantial content", [[President of Indonesia|Indonesian President]] [[Joko Widodo]] postpones the vote on a new criminal code,  intended to replace the century-old [[Indonesian criminal procedure#History_of_Indonesia's_criminal_procedure|Dutch colonial-era penal code]]. The proposed code would criminalise [[extramarital sex]], insults to the president and "obscene acts". [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/09/23/asia/indonesia-sex-code-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Civil Guard (Spain)|Spanish Civil Guard]] arrests nine members of the [[Committees for the Defense of the Republic|Committees for the Defence of the Catalan Republic]] for planning violent acts and creating homemade explosives. Expressions of support come from politicians including the [[Generalitat of Catalonia|Government]] and [[Quim Torra|President]] of [[Catalonia]] claiming the charges represent repression against Catalonia. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20190923/47570882252/guardia-civil-operacion-independentistas-cdr-detenidos-video-seo-ext.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
*[[2016 Notre-Dame de Paris bombing attempt]]
**A group of alleged [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] sympathisers go on trial in [[France]], including two women accused of an attempted [[car bomb]]ing at [[Notre-Dame Cathedral]] in 2016. Defendants also include a man being [[Trial in absentia|tried ''in absentia'']] whom the [[United States]] claims to have killed via drone strike in 2017; the court ruled no evidence had been provided to confirm his death. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190923-paris-notre-dame-female-suspected-jihadists-women-trial-botched-terror-attack-group (France 24)]
*In [[Port-au-Prince]], an [[Associated Press]] photojournalist and a security guard are wounded when [[2015–16 Haitian parliamentary election#List_of_elected_senators|Senator]] [[Jean Marie Ralph Féthière]] ([[Haitian Tèt Kale Party|PHTK]]) opens fire, reportedly trying to pass through a demonstration outside the [[Haitian Parliament]]. The [[Senate (Haiti)|Senate]] tries to convene and appoint [[Fritz-William Michel]] as [[Prime Minister of Haiti|Prime Minister]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/sep/23/haiti-shooting-senator-gun-parliament-photojournalist (''The Guardian'')]

;Sports
*The [[World Anti-Doping Agency]] launches a probe into "inconsistencies" with laboratory results from [[Russia]], promising "the most stringent sanctions" if violations are found. Russia was previously banned from the [[2018 Winter Olympics]] following a similar probe. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190923-world-sport-anti-doping-body-says-to-probe-russia-inconsistencies (France 24)]
